sentences.text: Two valid species exist within this genus: the North Island giant moa and the South Island giant moa.
Their bodies were covered in reddish-brown, hair-like feathers that spanned most of their surface.
They possessed a long neck and large, powerful feet, adaptations that allowed them to reach high vegetation.
Females may have been the tallest bird ever, reaching approximately 3.6 meters in height.
These females are estimated to have weighed between 230 and 278 kilograms.
Their eggs were enormous, roughly the size of a rugby ball and 80 times the volume of a chicken egg.
Richard Owen formally described the genus Dinornis in the year 1843.
Dietary adaptations included long necks and broad, sharp beaks suited for eating vegetation from subalpine herbs to tree branches.
Males likely incubated these massive eggs for up to three months before hatching.
Chicks were able to see, run, and feed themselves immediately after hatching.
Māori hunters drove the birds into holes and stole their nests to harvest them.
This animal was endemic to New Zealand.
The time range for Dinornis extends from 0.129 million years ago to the present Holocene.
Fossils of this group date from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene.
Before humans arrived, the population remained stable in New Zealand for at least 40,000 years.
All species of Dinornis went extinct by the year 1500.
Polynesian settlers wiped out the population by hunting them for food.
